issues.description: Method name mismatch in ArrayHelpers: the template's ArrayHelpers class defines a method named appendElement(T[] array, T element) (template repository), but Stock.java in the template calls ArrayHelpers.addElementToArray(...). The solution repository uses addElementToArray(T[] array, T element). This inconsistent identifier/name for the same utility method causes a compilation error when building the template and prevents students from running the project.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the ArrayHelpers API consistent between template and solution. Rename the method in the template from appendElement(...) to addElementToArray(T[] array, T element) (matching the solution and usages in Stock.java), or alternatively change all calls to use appendElement. Preferred fix: update template/src/de/tum/cit/ase/ArrayHelpers.java to provide public static <T> T[] addElementToArray(T[] array, T element) with the same behavior and adjust any references if needed so the project compiles.

issues.description: The array helper that appends an element to an array is named inconsistently across artifacts. In the template ArrayHelpers class the method is declared as appendElement(T[] array, T element) but the template Stock class calls ArrayHelpers.addElementToArray(...). The solution repository defines the helper as addElementToArray(T[] array, T element). Because the concept is the same (a helper to add an element to an array), students cannot clearly map the requirement to the template code and will get a compilation error (undefined method) when using the provided template. This naming mismatch (appendElement vs addElementToArray) breaks the conceptual mapping and blocks straightforward compilation and comparison with the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the helper method name across artifacts so the same identifier is used everywhere. Recommended: rename the method in the template ArrayHelpers from appendElement(...) to addElementToArray(...) (matching the solution and the calls in Stock.java). Alternatively, change the call in the template Stock.java to ArrayHelpers.appendElement(...). Also ensure the problem statement references (if any) and any other usages are updated to the single chosen name (preferably addElementToArray to match the solution).
